findings.title: Key exchange: X25519MLKEM768, a hybrid of X25519 and ML-KEM-768
findings.detail: Negotiated by a client that offers post-quantum key exchange. The session keys depend on both parts, so they stay secret unless both are broken.

findings.title: Recorded traffic is protected only for clients that support post-quantum key exchange
findings.detail: Sessions that negotiate ML-KEM cannot be decrypted later by a quantum computer. Sessions from clients that fall back to classical key exchange can: an attacker who records them now can decrypt them once a large quantum computer exists ("harvest now, decrypt later"). Which of your clients fall back is not visible from outside.

learn.label: Watch a quantum attacker fail against hybrid

findings.title: A quantum computer could impersonate this server, but only at the time of an attack
findings.detail: The server’s identity rests on the certificate key (ECDSA P-256), a chain signature (ECDSA with SHA-256), a chain signature (ECDSA with SHA-384) and a chain signature (RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 with SHA-256). Shor’s algorithm recovers such private keys from the public keys, which would let an attacker present this identity. Unlike key exchange, this cannot be used on recorded traffic: the forgery has to be made, with a working quantum computer, during a live connection while the certificate is still valid. Publicly trusted certificate authorities do not issue post-quantum certificates yet, so a public site cannot change this alone today.

findings.title: Data is encrypted with AES-256-GCM
findings.detail: Cipher suite TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384. The key for it comes out of the key exchange above; the cipher itself uses no public-key cryptography.

evidence.label: Cipher suite
evidence.value: 0x1302 TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384

findings.title: The cipher is not at risk from a quantum computer
findings.detail: Quantum computers do not break symmetric ciphers. Grover’s algorithm at best halves the effective key length, which leaves a 256-bit key with about 128 bits of security.

findings.title: Cookie _ga can be sent over plain HTTP

findings.title: Internal dependencies cannot be observed from outside
findings.detail: Connections between your own services, databases, key storage, vendor APIs and the devices your users connect from all use cryptography too. None of it is visible to an external scan. Finding it is the first step of a migration.
